did_you_know.text: Isaiah describes a figure who will spring from the house of Jesse using two images from the plant world: a “shoot” growing from a stump and a “branch” blossoming from the roots.
The Spirit of the LORD will rest upon the figure described, and the verse lists six qualities: wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of the LORD.
The judge described will not judge merely by what his eyes see or decide only by what his ears hear.
He will judge the poor with righteousness and decide fairly for the humble of the earth; his words are described as having the power to strike the earth and put the wicked to death.
Righteousness and faithfulness are described as belts tied around his waist and hips, meaning they are constant foundations of his character and conduct.
The vision of peace includes animals that do not naturally live together: a wolf with a lamb, a leopard with a young goat, and a lion beside cattle.
In the situation described, even a baby will be able to play near a cobra’s hole and a viper’s nest without being harmed.
The reason for the peace described is that “the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD”; this knowledge is compared to waters covering the sea.
The root of Jesse is described as a “banner”—a raised signal—to which the nations will turn, and his resting place is described as glorious.
The LORD will gather the remnant of his people from many lands and regions, including Assyria, Egypt, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
